**Answer: 611 pieces**

**Setup.** Model each piece as an edge joining the apple it came from to the student who receives it. This gives a bipartite graph with 221 apple-vertices and 403 student-vertices, so 624 vertices in total. A connected component with a apples and b students must have a/b = 221/403 for the shares to be equal.

**Structure of the components.** Since gcd(221, 403) = 13 (because 221 = 13·17 and 403 = 13·31), the ratio reduces to 17:31. So every component contains a multiple of 17 apples and a multiple of 31 students, and each component has at least 17 apples. Therefore there are at most 221/17 = 13 components.

**Lower bound.** A connected graph on v vertices needs at least v − 1 edges. With at most 13 components, the number of pieces (edges) is at least

624 − 13 = 611.

**Achievability.** Split the material into 13 groups, each with 17 apples and 31 students. Within each group, cut the apples so that the 47 pieces form a spanning tree on the 48 vertices, with each student receiving 17/31 of an apple. This is possible for each group, so the bound is attained.

**Check with the general formula.** The minimum number of pieces for n apples shared equally among m students is m + n − gcd(m, n). Here that is 403 + 221 − 13 = 611, which agrees.

ANSWER: 611
